assessments.reasoning: Section 2.1.2 describes a square-bracketed sequence forming a quotation object and delaying execution of the surrounded code, with combinators taking quotation objects as parameters. Its chosen if example distinguishes constructing both quotations from executing a selected branch.

challenge.method: Compared construction and invocation using the two-branch example, and checked the separate parse-time word behavior in §2.3.1.
challenge.results: The reviewed claim concerns delayed evaluation of the quoted code. Parser dispatch and runtime quotation invocation are separate operations, and the paper does not say enclosing brackets disable parsing words.

limitations: The account treats a quotation as a first-class object. Other parse-time constructs and current release behavior are outside this claim.
